reproduction_target: panREPET: a reference-free Snakemake pipeline that detects TE insertions shared between de novo assembled genomes of a species by pairwise comparison. Applied to a Brachypodium distachyon pan-genome (54 -> 42 accessions after QC). Steps: TE reference-library build (TEdenovo/REPET on Bd21 v3.2) and TE annotation (panTEannot, a Snakemake re-implementation of REPET TEannot using Blaster/Censor/RepeatMasker); then panREPET proper: coverage-based TE-copy extraction (covcons), flanking-sequence extension (bedtools slop), reciprocal-best-hit detection (Minimap2 + Matcher), clique detection (NetworkX find_cliques), phylogenetic-distance computation (Biopython Phylo), and downstream ecogenome/climate statistics (Seaborn/statsmodels, kgc R package).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from the biorxiv v2 full-text Methods prose (fetched via curl; WebFetch/JATS 403-blocked). Two author code repos exist on ForgeMIA GitLab (panREPET, panTEannot); panREPET landing/README prose was read (stage1) and shows a Snakemake workflow driven by per-rule conda env specs (envs/*.yaml with exact tool pins: biopython=1.79, bedtools=2.30.0, minimap2=2.24) and, alternatively, a published Singularity image 'library://jconfais/repet/panrepet:1.0' bundling minimap/bedtools/matcher. The Singularity reference is TAG-pinned (:1.0), not digest-pinned, and the conda specs are env files (python>=3.5 floating, no channel/build lock) — not lockfiles. Both are CLAIMS only at stage1 (not executed, not validated), so version axis is capped at 1 and all verdicts are capped at RI. No custom-script line reading was performed (stage2). No wet-lab steps (public genome data reuse), so W=0.

steps.label: TE reference-library build with TEdenovo (REPET package, Flutre et al. 2011) from the Bd21 v3.2 genome; library also distributed via RepetDB - no REPET version pinned in prose/repo

panTEannot TE annotation (Snakemake re-implementation of REPET TEannot; similarity search via Blaster, Censor, RepeatMasker) - separate ForgeMIA repo exists; REPET/RepeatMasker versions not pinned in prose
panREPET Step 1: extract TE copies by coverage percentage (covcons parameter) - custom python in panREPET repo, conda env envs/biopython.yaml (biopython=1.79), covcons set in config/example.yaml
panREPET Step 2: add flanking genomic sequence via bedtools slop - envs/bedtools.yaml pins bedtools=2.30.0; also in Singularity image

panREPET Step 3: bidirectional (reciprocal) best-hit detection via Minimap2 (Li 2018) then Matcher (Quesneville et al. 2003) - envs/minimap2.yaml pins minimap2=2.24; Matcher provided via Singularity image (no standalone version)
panREPET Step 4: TE-insertion clique detection with NetworkX version 2.4 (read_edgelist + find_cliques) - version stated in prose (not in shown conda envs)
Phylogenetic pairwise-distance computation between accessions using the Biopython Phylo module (biopython=1.79 pinned in repo conda envs)

Downstream ecogenome/climate statistics and figures: clustermaps (Seaborn), ANOVA (statsmodels, python 3.10.13), climate-class assignment (kgc R package v1.0.0.2) - analysis/figure scripts not clearly provided in the pipeline repo; Seaborn/statsmodels versions floating

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 5/8 computational steps — the panREPET-proper pipeline (covcons extraction, bedtools slop, Minimap2+Matcher reciprocal-best-hit, NetworkX find_cliques, Biopython Phylo), which are backed by an author Snakemake repo with per-rule conda env specs (biopython=1.79, bedtools=2.30.0, minimap2=2.24) and a published Singularity image bundling minimap/bedtools/matcher. 3/8 steps cap at NI: TEdenovo library build (C1) and panTEannot annotation (C2) because their REPET/RepeatMasker tool versions are unpinned, and downstream statistics (C8) because figure/stat scripts are not clearly provided and Seaborn/statsmodels versions are floating. R★ not assignable at stage1. The Singularity image is TAG-pinned (:1.0) not digest-pinned and the conda specs are env files without lock closure — both are unvalidated claims, so no step exceeds RI without an executed environment capture in stage2.
headline.coverage: 8 computational steps assessed from biorxiv v2 Methods prose plus panREPET README/Snakefile/conda-env prose. No wet-lab steps (public de novo assemblies reused), so W=0.

gaps.where: Whole pipeline environment (panREPET repo: Snakefile conda directives + Singularity image)
gaps.missing: Reproducibility rests on per-rule conda env files (envs/*.yaml) and a Singularity image 'library://jconfais/repet/panrepet:1.0'. The env files pin tool versions (biopython=1.79, bedtools=2.30.0, minimap2=2.24) but declare 'python >= 3.5' (floating) with no channel/build lock; the Singularity reference is tag-pinned (:1.0), not a content digest. No conda-lock/pixi lockfile or container digest is provided. All of this is a CLAIM only at stage1 (not executed/validated).
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a resolved lockfile (conda-lock or pixi) and/or a digest-pinned container (Singularity SIF checksum / OCI sha256) covering every tool plus system dependencies, and have stage2 execute it to validate the environment capture.

gaps.where: C1 TEdenovo (REPET), C2 panTEannot (Blaster/Censor/RepeatMasker), and Matcher (C5)
gaps.missing: REPET-family tool versions (TEdenovo, TEannot, Blaster, Censor, RepeatMasker, Matcher) are cited by reference but not version-pinned in prose; Matcher is only available inside the Singularity image with no standalone version. Downstream Seaborn/statsmodels versions are also absent (C8).
gaps.how_to_close: Record exact versions (and builds) for all REPET-family tools and the downstream Python plotting/stats packages in Methods or a versions table / conda env.

gaps.where: Input genome assemblies and TE library (Data availability)
gaps.missing: Data availability names live databases without versioned accessions: 53 B. distachyon de novo assemblies + annotations from Phytozome (generic https://phytozome.jgi.doe.gov/, Gordon et al. 2017), BdTR7a from Stritt et al. 2019, and the Bd21 TE library/annotation from RepetDB. Specific per-accession genome versions are only loosely referenced (Supplementary Table 1); no accession list with fixed versions/DOIs is given.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide an explicit accession/version table (or a deposited snapshot/DOI) for every genome assembly and the exact RepetDB TE-library release used.

gaps.missing: RepetDB (urgi.versailles.inrae.fr/repetdb) and Phytozome are live, versioned-over-time databases pulled without a pinned snapshot; contents can change, so retrieval is not deterministic. (Note: the generic Phytozome URL in the paper now fails to resolve — content migrated to phytozome-next.jgi.doe.gov.)
gaps.how_to_close: Record the database release/date-stamped export used, or deposit the retrieved TE library and genome set as a fixed archive (Zenodo/figshare) with a DOI.
